sentences.text: 4. The revisionist was a milkman and on 22.6.2001 at 9 a.m. was stopped by the Food Inspector and asked about the milk to which he disclosed that the same is for public sale for human consumption and was carrying three cans of mixed milk of buffalo and cow being 30 litre.
The license was asked on which he refused.
On suspicion of the same being adulterated, the milk was homogenized and 750 ml.
was purchased, proceedings were done, the sample was sealed and then sent to food analyst for it's test.
The public analyst vide his report dated 20.7.2001 stated of the sample to be containing milt fat 4.5% and milk solids not fat to be 4.0 % and opined that the milk solids not fat was less by 53 %.
The proceedings were initiated against the revisionist on which the trial took place and he was convicted and sentenced by the trial court as stated above.

The accused preferred an appeal against the judgement and order of conviction being Criminal Appeal No.63 of 2011 (Khaleel Ahmad Vs.
State of U.P.) which was dismissed vide judgement and order dated 28.7.2012 passed by the Vth Addl. Sessions Judge, Bijnor upholding the judgement and order of conviction dated 10.8.2011.

sentences.text: The present revision has thus been filed against the said judgement and orders before this Court.
5. Learned counsel for the revisionist argued that the revisionist has been falsely implicated in the present case.
It is submitted that the revisionist has denied being a seller of milk and doing the said work.
He further submitted that even the revisionist submitted that there are many other persons in the village by the name of Khaleel and the revisionist has been implicated falsely on mis-identity.

It is further submitted that even the report of the public analyst goes to show that the sample was only deficient for milk solids not fat whereas the milk fat was found to be as per the prescribed standard and there was no other extraneous material present in the sample which would have made the same to be unfit for human consumption, injuries or noxious.
It is submitted that the courts failed to consider the said aspects and have illegally convicted the revisionist.
It is submitted that the revisionist has been convicted for rigorous imprisonment for a term of seven months with fine and default punishment being simple imprisonment.
As a matter of fact the revisionist has gone about six months of imprisonment out of the imprisonment of seven months as awarded to him.

It is further submitted that the revisionist was on bail during trial which was not misused by him and further after grant of bail to him in the present revision vide order dated 1.2.2013 he has not misused the said liberty.
It is further argued that the revisionist is aged about 53 years as of now as he has given his age as 40 years in his statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. which was recorded on 31.3.2011.

It is submitted that as such looking to the period of incarceration and the sentence as awarded since the revisionist has already undergone the minimum sentence as per the Act, the sentence be reduced to the period already undergone by him.
6. Learned counsel for the State has been heard.
7. After having heard learned counsel for the parties and perusing the record, it is evident that the sample in the present case was drawn on 22.6.2001 and 23 years since then have passed.
The conviction of the revisionist by the trial court is dated 10.8.2011, 13 years since then have passed, the appeal has been decided on 28.7.2012, 12 years since then have passed.

At the time of incident, the Khaleel Ahmad vs State Of U.P. on 17 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156275177/

sentences.text: As of now he is aged about 53 years.

From the perusal of order dated 1.2.2013 by which he was granted bail by another Bench of this Court in present revision, it is clear that he has undergone about six months of imprisonment, the said order reads as under:-
"Heard learned counsel for the revisionist and learned A.G.A.
The present criminal revision has been filed against the Judgement and order dated 28.7.2012 passed by Vth Additional Sessions Judge, Bijnor in Criminal Appeal No.63 of 2011 a s also the order dated 10.8.2011 passed by the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Nagina, Bijnor in Case No. 203 of 2002, whereby the revisionist has been convicted and sentenced, under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,
for seven months rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs.1500/- and in default in payment of fine to undergo further one month additional simple imprisonment.
It is contended by learned counsel for the revisionist that the revisionist was on bail during trial and he has not misused the liberty of bail.
It is further contended that the revision is not likely to be heard in near future and the revisionist has already undergone about six months of imprisonment.
Learned A.G.A. did not raise any dispute with regard to the aforesaid facts.
Admit.
List for hearing in due course.

Without expressing any opinion on merits of the case and considering the facts and circumstances of the case, let the revisionist Khaleel Ahmad be released on bail in the offence he has been convicted and sentenced as aforesaid, on his furnishing a personal bond and two local sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned.
As soon as personal and surety bonds are furnished, photocopies of the same are directed to be transmitted to this Court forthwith by the concerned court to be kept on record.
Realization of fine to the extent of 50% shall be kept in abeyance during the pendency of the present revision.
It is made clear that the half of the amount of fine shall be deposited by the revisionist within 15 days from the date of release.
In case, the half of the amount of fine is not deposited, then this bail order shall be deemed cancelled."

8. The Apex Court in the case of Nand Lal Vs. State of Uttarakhand : (2010) 4 SCC 562 has held that the valid grounds for reduction of the sentence are the delay in proceedings and age of the accused.

3 Looking to the facts it transpires that the incident has taken place almost 23 years ago, the revisionist is now 53 years of age and that out of the conviction of seven months as awarded to him by the trial court, he has undergone about six months and has also deposited half of the fine.
9. The present revision is allowed to the extent that while maintaining the conviction of the revisionist, his sentence is reduced to the period already undergone.
10. The revisionist is on bail.
His bail bonds are cancelled and sureties discharged.
He need not surrender if not wanted in any other case.
11. Office is directed to transmit the copy of this judgement along with the trial court records to the concerned trial court forthwith for its compliance and necessary action.
( Samit Gopal, J.) Order Date :- 17.5.2024
